answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a jetty, answers an onyx, and is named by a raven: a farm can mint raven bindings instantly, but the jetty behind each one is disk, and the onyx will catch the ones that share it. The attacker therefore pays for real storage per head.
